status_reason: the gate rests on the von Reyn 2014 Fig. 1 caption, read once and not re-readable in the 2026-09-24 check (main text paywalled); the von Reyn 2014 loom start/end size and elevation are still unread; the encoder saturation constants and the stimulus elevation need owner review before this is preregistered
summary: Frontal dark looming disc at five approach speeds: does the Giant Fiber spike more often for faster looms (lower r/v), as the GF-mediated short-mode takeoff fraction does in flies, and never without a stimulus?

stimulus.geometry: frontal (azimuth 0), both eyes driven equally; elevation effects (Dombrovski et al., bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.09.04.610846) are not modelled
stimulus.literature_match: r/v set and per-condition n from von Reyn 2014 Fig. 1; start size 10 deg as in Jang 2023 (10 to 63 deg), von Reyn 2017 and Klapoetke 2017 (10 to 90 deg); Ache 2019 behaviour looms 10 to 90 deg at 11 deg elevation, 50 deg azimuth (read via summary, not verbatim); von Reyn 2014 start/end sizes still not verified

encoder.assumption: division of labour from von Reyn 2017 / Ache 2019 (qualitative). i_max equals the WP5 encoder amplitude. Ramp end points are declared engineering choices, set before any run and never tuned. No direct DNp01 drive.

decoder.rule: GF-mediated (short-mode) takeoff = at least one DNp01 spike from loom onset to post-window end

seed_role: encoder per-cell noise; network starts from rest every trial

gates.claim: The fraction of looms evoking a GF spike falls with log10(r/v) (slope 95% CI below 0).
gates.basis: published: short-mode (GF-driven) takeoff fraction declines linearly with log(r/v), R^2 = 0.903, n = 660 flies

gates.claim: No GF spike in any sham trial (encoder runs, nothing delivered).
gates.basis: causal control of the model itself; not a literature value

reported.claim: GF-spike fraction pooled over r/v 14, 40, 70 ms vs the published short-mode fraction 95/450 = 0.21.
reported.basis: reported only: the published fraction is among flies that took off, the simulated one is per loom; for comparison Ache 2019 control flies: 26% [47/178] short-mode (TNT control) and 17% [18/105] (Kir2.1 control), r/v mix differs

reported.claim: GF-spike fraction to a receding disc.
reported.basis: report only; no published GF response to receding looms was found. Related: LPLC2 'did not respond to dark receding looming or to luminance-matched motion-free darkening stimulus' (Klapoetke 2017, calcium imaging), which predicts little GF drive; not gated

decision_rule: Behaviour PASS iff every gate passes. Physiology PASS iff every check lies in its bound. Verdict PASS iff both pass on a confirmatory run (real graph, this spec committed and unchanged, these seeds, clean tree); PASS_PROVISIONAL if any gating value is marked unverified; FAIL if any gate or check fails; INCONCLUSIVE if one cannot be evaluated. Full rule: validation/harness.py VERDICTS.

vonreyn2014.citation: von Reyn CR, et al., Card GM (2014) A spike-timing mechanism for action selection. Nat Neurosci 17:962-970
vonreyn2014.read: Fig. 1 caption and abstract (earlier check); supplementary PDF (this check). Main text paywalled, not re-read.
values_read: short/long takeoff split at 6.87 ms wing-raise+jump duration; pooled r/v 14, 40, 70 ms: 95 short vs 355 long (n = 450)
short-mode fraction declines linearly with log(r/v): slope -19.27 (units as printed), R^2 = 0.903; n = 108, 115, 202, 133, 102 flies at r/v 8, 14, 40, 70, 140 ms
a GF spike forces a short-mode takeoff; the GF has a higher activation threshold than the parallel pathways (abstract)
Supp. Fig. 5: GF whole-cell example spike responses (from 10 flies) and subthreshold responses (from 33 flies) to looms at three r/v
Supp. Fig. 3a: takeoff percentages across r/v 14, 40, 70 ms compared by chi-square (P = 0.015, 0.087, 0.148); percentages shown only as bars

vonreyn2017.citation: von Reyn CR, et al., Card GM (2017) Feature integration drives probabilistic behavior in the Drosophila escape response. Neuron 94:1190-1204
values_read: LC4 conveys angular velocity, LPLC2 angular size; the GF integrates them (qualitative; encoder assumption)
'looming stimuli generate GF spikes in only a small subset of tethered flies'
'Both single GF spikes and GF-mediated takeoffs occur, on average, at a fixed delay after a looming disk surpasses 39 deg'

ache2019.citation: Ache JM, et al., Card GM (2019) Neural basis for looming size and velocity encoding in the Drosophila giant fiber escape pathway. Curr Biol 29:1073-1081
values_read: LC4 (velocity) and LPLC2 (size) inputs to the GF, summed approximately linearly (qualitative; encoder assumption)
GF recordings kept if resting potential below -55 mV; only trials without a GF action potential analysed
short-mode takeoffs: TNT control 26% [47/178] vs LPLC2-silenced 3% [3/93]; Kir2.1 control 17% [18/105] vs 7% [5/70] (Figs 1C-D)

jang2023.citation: Jang H, Goodman DP, Ausborn J, von Reyn CR (2023) Azimuthal invariance to looming stimuli in the Drosophila giant fiber escape circuit. J Exp Biol 226(8):jeb244790
values_read: GF accepted if resting potential less than -50 mV; looms 10 to 63 deg at r/v 10, 20, 40, 80 ms

klapoetke2017.citation: Klapoetke NC, et al., Reiser MB (2017) Ultra-selective looming detection from radial motion opponency. Nature 551:237-241
values_read: LPLC2 measured by calcium imaging only (no Hz)
'LPLC2 neurons did not respond to dark receding looming or to luminance-matched motion-free darkening stimulus'
